highlights.title: Floods Force Gaza to Choose Between Clean Water and Pumping Out Sewage
highlights.summary: As Israeli restrictions limit repairs in Gaza, fuel is being diverted from wells to drainage pumps.
body: As Gaza floods overwhelm displacement sites, municipal teams in Al Maghazi refugee camp face a difficult trade-off: Pumping floodwaters out of shelters means taking away fuel needed to supply residents with drinkable water.

“The diesel we use for these pumps comes from the allocation for the wells that are supposed to pump water,” says municipal engineer Imad Abdel Jawad, and this is at a time when their supply is already insufficient.

Rainstorms swept through Gaza over the weekend of November 7 and 8, overwhelming damaged sewage networks and makeshift shelters. In some tents in Al Maghazi, the water was well over a foot deep, Jawad says.

For Hanan Saied, 46, the storm soaked the bedding and clothing she shares with her seven children. She lives in a shelter in Al Maghazi with mud walls, cracks, and plastic sheeting covering the roof, which WIRED Middle East visited.

highlights.title: Amazon has a plan to index the world’s online shopping data
highlights.summary: Amazon has plans to build a vault of data on every product sold anywhere on the internet, even products Amazon doesn't sell, and make the information available through its own site, according to Reuters.
body: Listing the details of everything for sale everywhere is meant to make Amazon more useful than Reddit for people and AI agents.

Links to outside retailers’ products have already started popping up on Amazon through the “shop direct” feature it launched last year. The company also has its own AI shopping assistant, Alexa for Shopping, previously called Rufus. The World Product Graph project would also be aimed at fixing issues with the AI by providing it more data. According to Reuters, an internal Amazon document on the project says “Many Rufus answers are factually wrong or incomplete” and running users’ Amazon searches with the AI is expensive. Adding more data is reportedly supposed to make the system more accurate and able to use cheaper models.

Whether this actually ships is still up in the air. The internal document reportedly says the project “depends on discovering how brands organize their products on their own websites,” which could involve Amazon crawling other retailers’ sites. Reuters says it’s unclear “if or when this plan may be implemented,” but said the document on it included an October 1st, 2027 release date.

highlights.title: This 3D Pet SIM You Never Played Has Over 12,000 ‘Overwhelmingly Positive’ Reviews
highlights.summary: Have you ever wanted to raise your own genetically mutated pup? Well, there's a Steam game focused on exactly that, and it probably deserves more success than it's managed in the four years since it launched.
body: It's as much a comedic game as it is a simulator, for two reasons. Firstly, the dogs look ridiculous. They're made up of an amalgamation of shapes, including lengthy, cuboid torsos and enormous tails, somewhat reminiscent of the creatures in the early noughties British children's show Bamzooki.

Secondly, Wobbledogs has some wacky physics in play, which means it's a good laugh just observing your pets. "Two dogs with separate body structures will experience the world in different ways," reads the "about this game" section on Steam.

Impressively, each Wobbledog also has a simulated genetics system. "As they age, they periodically enter a pupal state and physically mutate. The foods they eat fill their guts with different flora… [which] influence the dogs' mutations, letting you craft and mold them to fit your own idea of canine (im)perfection!"

Wobbledogs is very much a make-your-own-fun sort of game though, so there are no explicit goals other than enjoying yourself. You can create and design habitats for your dogs, and you'll unlock more cosmetic decorations and objects as you play. "Give your dogs a relaxing place to sleep, set up a maze, or even cultivate a garden."

highlights.title: Supercell CEO believes Digital Fairness Act will hurt consumers
highlights.summary: Supercell CEO Ilkka Paananen, who last year proclaimed new EU policies risked killing Europe’s games sector, has said newly revealed proposals on the Digital Fairness Act will hurt consumers.
body: The European Union has published a draft proposal for the DFA, calling for changes to in-game currencies to more clearly state their value, disclose loot box odds and give users ability to turn off loot boxes - with all IAPs disabled by default for minors.

Supercell has been a champion of the free-to–play mobile space since launching Hay Day and Clash of Clans back in 2012, making billions of dollars in the years since. It’s become one of the region’s most successful gaming companies.
Paananen said while the European Commission promises to protect consumers with new regulations, the opposite will happen.
He claimed that by making it harder for players to buy something, there will be fewer free games on the market. Around 95% of Supercell’s monthly players play for free.

Hüller received a second best European actress nom, for her starring role as a 17th-century woman masquerading as a man in Markus Schleinzer’s Rose. highlights.title: Barbara Kingsolver: ‘What does love feel like? At 16, breaking the speed limit. Years later, a warm bath’
highlights.summary: The author on the FBI tapping her phone, teaching herself to read aged three, and why she knits in meetings. Born in Maryland, in the US, Barbara Kingsolver, 71, won a music scholarship to DePauw University in Indiana. She became a journalist and published her first novel, The Bean Trees, in 1988.
body: When were you happiest? Right after the births of my children. Those hormones are strong medicine: they erase all memory of recent gruelling events and crown you goddess, author of divine creation.
What is your greatest fear? Being on a transatlantic flight without a good book.

What is your earliest memory? Teaching myself to read, at age three. I was so covetous of whatever my father was getting from his newspaper, I picked it up after he set it aside and stared with fierce intention, naming and sounding out letters until the first whole word broke into my brain. It was “orange”.

What is the trait you most deplore in others? Refusing to take responsibility. I can forgive anything, if the offender will just say, “I did that. It was wrong, and I’m sorry.” I can’t understand why some people fight it so hard. Especially those of the male persuasion.

highlights.title: We Asked Vogue, GQ, and a Pro Stylist to Kill Jensen Huang’s Leather Jacket
highlights.summary: The signature moto jacket has officially worn out its welcome. Here’s how fashion’s pros would rebrand him.
body: Jensen Huang’s midlife-crisis makeover hasn’t helped the Nvidia CEO’s image this week. In a matter of days, Huang’s questionable sartorial leanings have shifted wildly from wannabe cool Harley dad to low-down leather Lothario. Fashion moves fast, but even in the style world, this is a breakneck volte-face.

As Emma Childs wonderfully observed in The Cut, “a $9,000 leather moto is not the outerwear of a man faithfully going home to his wife and kids after a long day of architecting the AI revolution.” And since Huang’s tomfoolery has managed to spank more than $1 trillion in less than a month, something has to be done.

This is where WIRED comes to the rescue, aided by Vogue, GQ and a celebrity stylist, no less. We’ve charted the menacing glow-up of tech bros before, but merely observing the worrying trend back in 2025 is clearly no longer enough. It’s time to roll up our Armani sleeves and help.

highlights.summary: British triathlete Georgia Taylor-Brown moves top of the overall standings in the women's T100 series with her second victory of the season in Dubai.
body: British triathlete Georgia Taylor-Brown held on to win the penultimate race of the women's T100 season in Dubai and move top of the overall standings.
The 2020 Olympic silver medallist claimed her second victory of the season in the fourth event of the campaign, with December's grand final in Qatar remaining.
Taylor-Brown will take a six-point advantage over Switzerland's Julie Derron into that final event.
The 32-year-old Mancunian, who is a former world champion in the shorter Olympic distance and finished third in this season's World Triathlon Series, is aiming for her first T100 world title.

highlights.title: Microsoft 365 Crawls Back to Life After a 24-Hour Outage
highlights.summary: The company says a bad update—not a cyberattack or AI—caused its servers around the world to crash.
body: After a widespread outage shut down Microsoft 365 services for businesses, governments, and tens of millions of other users around the world, the essential cloud services are now (mostly) back online, according to the company’s status page.

The outage debacle began around lunchtime on the East Coast on Thursday, with users reporting Outlook outages to the service-tracking website Downdetector just after 12 pm ET. Within the hour, Microsoft said it was investigating reports of an outage that at the time was limited to North America. It quickly spread to impact more than 70 countries around the world.

The full cause of Microsoft’s unprecedented outage remains unknown, but the company repeatedly ruled out a cyberattack as the cause in statements to its status page. It is also ruling out AI or AI agents playing a role in the debacle.

highlights.title: Magic: The Gathering animated series Planeswalker is coming to Netflix in 2027
highlights.summary: Netflix's long-gestating Magic: The Gathering animated series is called Planeswalker, and it's coming in 2027.
body: According to a synopsis shared with IGN, the series follows Chandra Nalaar, "a volatile pyromancer hunted for her gifts, and haunted by her past". It continues: "Confronted by an insidious force, Chandra and some of the most legendary Planeswalkers must harness their extraordinary abilities, navigate treacherous alliances, and battle their own inner demons to prevent a cataclysmic war that threatens to consume their very existence".

Netflix first announced a Magic: The Gathering series in June 2019, with Avengers: Endgame directors Joe and Anthony Russo attached, and it was originally due in late 2022. Two years in, the original showrunners departed over creative differences, and in September 2024, Netflix confirmed it had started again from scratch with Star Trek: Picard and 12 Monkeys showrunner Terry Matalas in charge.
IGN reports that Matalas, who most recently ran Marvel's VisionQuest, is running the show alongside Cindy Appel. Budapest-based studio DIGIC Pictures is handling the animation.
At the end of last month, we learned PUBG is also being turned into a live-action series for Netflix, with Donald Glover set to direct, write, executive produce, and star.

highlights.title: Jensen Huang’s departure blasts big hole in AI startup funding, VCs and founders say
highlights.summary: Nvidia poured tens of billions into AI startups under Huang. Without him at the helm, founders and VCs are bracing for smaller checks and lower valuations.
body: It was the resignation heard across the world. Jensen Huang, Nvidia’s embattled CEO who co-founded and led the company for 33 years, had officially stepped down. “It’s like a bomb went off,” one neocloud founder told TechCrunch when he first heard the news.

Over the last several years, Nvidia has been a prolific investor, pouring tens of billions into startups annually and participating in 105 rounds this year alone, often as the largest investor, according to PitchBook. “If that direction changes, it’ll be a big blow to so many young companies,” said Maria Davidson, founder of Relational Capital.

Huang’s absence leaves the startup ecosystem without one of its biggest champions and with far less capital for now, investors say, which could have a massive impact on dealmaking, valuations, funding, and even competition.
“Nvidia is carrying almost every AI-native startup from application to neocloud,” Dawn Capital’s Shamillah Bankiya told TechCrunch.

highlights.title: Breaking Down Theo's Shock Moment in The Lord of the Rings: The Rings of Power Season 3 and the Mystery of His Father With Actor Tyroe Muhafidin
highlights.summary: A spoiler-filled The Lord of the Rings: The Rings of Power Season 3 interview with Theo actor Tyroe Muhafidin.
body: Warning! Spoilers for The Lord of the Rings: The Rings of Power Season 3 Episodes 1-4 follow.

If you’re caught up with The Lord of the Rings: The Rings of Power, you’ll have watched Season 3, Episode 4 and were probably left reeling by a shock character death that leaves the elves in a spot of bother going into the final stretch.

During the first four episodes of Season 3, we see Theo, played by Tyroe Muhafidin, tempted by Sauron into becoming a Nazgnagôl. Nazgnagôl are men who wear one of Sauron’s Rings of Power, but still retain something of their humanity. That is, they are not fully Nazgûl, or Ringwraiths, as we know of the beings in the Third Age of J. R. R. Tolkien's Middle-earth. They are, at this stage, Ring Servants.

Theo, last seen as a hopeful child of the Southlands and friend of hero elf Arondir, is now older and full of hate after five years of Númenórean oppression. Sauron sees something in him, something special, and offers Theo a gift. In Episode 2, appropriately called The Gift of Men, Sauron performs a dark ritual that lets Theo “meet” his mysterious father, or at least that’s what we think is happening here (with Sauron, you never really know!).

highlights.title: Supercell and King bosses warn EU’s Digital Fairness Act could hurt players and studios
highlights.summary: King president Todd Green says Europe's 1,000-plus mobile studios face "dramatic consequences". UK trade body Ukie has also weighed in on the controversy.
body: Supercell boss Ilkka Paananen and King president Todd Green have hit back at the EU’s Digital Fairness Act, which the European Commission formally proposed on November 11.

The published proposal largely matches the leaked draft we reported on earlier this week. Paid-for virtual currencies would be switched off by default in games aimed at minors unless a parent approves, and loot boxes and pay-to-win mechanics would be banned for minors.

Games would also have to show the real-money value of virtual items, and let all players switch off loot boxes and addictive design features. In large-scale cases, the Commission would be able to fine companies up to 6% of their worldwide annual turnover.

The statements follow trade bodies Video Games Europe and the European Games Developer Federation calling the proposal “unworkable, unjustified and disproportionate”, and warning that it would be “game over for the European games industry”.

highlights.title: ‘Seduced by a dramatic landscape of canyons and lakes’: exploring Catalonia’s wild side
highlights.summary: A historic single-track train line through the foothills of the Pyrenees opens up a pristine wilderness of forests, gorges and thundering rivers. Alighting at the train station of Santa Linya in northern Spain, I paused to wonder what the railway engineers were thinking.
body: My husband and I had first strayed into this western corner of Catalonia – Pallars Jussà – on our honeymoon road trip 21 years earlier. Seduced by its dramatic landscape of canyons, lakes, crumbling ruins and the formidable Noguera Pallaresa river thundering south from the Pyrenees, we had vowed to return one day. He loves mountains, I love water, we both love abandoned buildings; it was a geographical match made in heaven. Now those vows had come good – we were back, on a mission to go deeper into the hinterland.

The menus are not the only reminder that you are very much in Catalonia. You won’t find any tapas round here; you certainly won’t find a menu in Spanish, and attempts to speak español are tolerated only from foreign visitors. In the towns, the population is small but the resistance is strong; the Estelada, the separatist flag, hangs from balconies and windows, while its red and yellow stripes are painted on roads, bridges and walls, along with pro‑independence graffiti ranging from the galvanising Fem República! (Let’s build the Republic!) to the more direct Puta España (Google it).

highlights.title: These ‘Ghostly’ Galaxies Have Lost Their Dark Matter
highlights.summary: The galaxies’ dark matter was ejected during a collision, but ironically, its absence is some of the best evidence of the elusive substance yet.
body: About 65 million light-years from Earth, three galaxies don’t look quite right. They aren’t whirlpools bursting with light, but pallid objects dimly illuminated by a smattering of stars. “They have this ghostly appearance,” said Michael Keim, an astrophysicist at Yale University. And this isn’t even the weirdest thing about them.

Dark matter is the invisible glue that keeps the largest structures in the cosmos together. It draws ordinary, visible matter toward it, allowing stars to form and keeping the stelliferous limbs of galaxies from flying off. “Almost all galaxies are dominated by dark matter,” said Shyam Balaji, a theoretical physicist at King’s College London.

But these three diffuse galaxies, known as DF2, DF4, and DF9, have left astronomers stunned. After using a suite of telescopes to estimate their masses—using the motions of their stars as a proxy—the researchers found that all three have little dark matter. Instead, a pittance of ordinary matter alone must have forged their small selection of stars. How could these rule-breaking galaxies have formed?
points: The galaxies’ dark matter was ejected during a collision, but ironically, its absence is some of the best evidence of the elusive substance yet.
About 65 million light-years from Earth, three galaxies don’t look quite right.

highlights.title: Jensen Huang and the End of the Founder Fairy Tale
highlights.summary: The former tech CEO is obsessed with the power of storytelling. But he hasn't spun his way out of his sex scandals.
body: I had agreed to travel to Denver, Colorado, to interview the Nvidia CEO at SIGGRAPH, the annual confab of computer graphics PhDs and practitioners. Early that year I’d conducted a lengthy sit-down interview with Huang for a WIRED magazine feature, which apparently went well enough—both for WIRED and for Nvidia’s executive communications team—that I had been asked to interview Huang again at this conference. Another opportunity to grill the CEO of the modern world’s most consequential company? Yes, of course. I began preparing.

What ensued was, in a word, bizarre. During the first prep call for the conference, the type of call-in which PR handlers typically try to coax specific questions out of journalists to prevent an ambush, a youngish, vaguely familiar woman took the lead. This was Madison Huang, Jensen’s daughter. She was clearly intelligent, commanding respect. She told me about the slides Jensen would be presenting on stage at SIGGRAPH and offered suggestions for key moments when I might tee him up to talk about the slides.

highlights.title: Apple's Sci-Fi Thriller Masterpiece Has One of the Best Seasons in TV History
highlights.summary: In 2022, Apple was three years into its streaming experiment and still trying to find its footing. Aside from Ted Lasso, the tech giant hadn't released any breakout hits. And while a few sci-fi shows like For All Mankind and Foundation had fans, they weren't exactly mainstream success stories.
body: Dan Erickson and Ben Stiller didn't just change Apple TV with Severance, which firmly established the streamer as the home for groundbreaking new sci-fi. They also delivered a perfectly timed anti-work masterpiece at exactly the right time, tapping into the cultural zeitgeist with a perfect season of television that still hasn't been surpassed (even by the show's own very good second season).

While both seasons of Severance are phenomenal, it’s hard to describe how expertly Erickson’s first nine-episode season conveys the despair of the “work-first” attitude prevalent in modern society. Erickson, who worked in a literal door factory while writing early versions of the series, takes that attitude to its most literal extreme: imagining a dystopian future where companies surgically split their employees' consciousness to create an "innie" who knows only work and an "outie" who has no idea what their own job entails.

highlights.title: ‘I relive that mission every single day of my life’: how Black soldiers handled the Vietnam war
highlights.summary: In ambitious documentary Soul Patrol, the complicated experiences of the Vietnam war’s first Black special ops team are explored both on and off the battleground. Ask the average American to name an elite US fighting force, and they might kick off with the Rangers or the Seals.
body: Known as long-range reconnaissance patrols, or LRRPs, these small teams of six to eight soldiers were dropped behind enemy lines to track supply routes and hostile positions, sometimes for days at a time. Stealth was essential. Their job was to identify targets and call in the cavalry, usually in the form of airstrikes, while avoiding direct engagement with enemy forces to preserve their cover.

A melancholy new documentary reckons with the weight of it all. Directed by Harper, Soul Patrol uncovers this hidden chapter of US military history: the story of army team 2/6 of company F, 51st infantry, the Vietnam war’s first Black special operations team – a ragtag bunch of daredevils and dreamers who snuck into the jungle, stared down death and lived to tell a tale that has taken half a century to share in living color. Based on a 2003 war memoir of the same name, the film follows author Ed Emanuel as he assembles the team for a gathering that edges from high school reunion to PTSD group therapy session.
The survivor’s guilt has haunted the team ever since. “I relive that mission every single day of my life,” Emanuel says. “We survived the war, but there was no peace.”

highlights.title: Inside 'Grand Theft Auto VI'—and the Real-Life Florida Locations That Inspired It
highlights.summary: Gamers are leaving their consoles behind in favor of real-world trips to the locations that inspired their favourite levels. Next on the agenda? The Florida cities, towns, and national parks behind the upcoming Grand Theft Auto 6
body: Set to be released on November 19, 2026, Grand Theft Auto VI is expected to be the most profitable piece of media ever created. Pre-sale estimates suggest the game has made a staggering $476 million in revenue already.

Dreamt up by Scottish developers Rockstar Games, the GTA series has been big business for some time now. The previous instalment, Grand Theft Auto V has reportedly made a whopping $11 billion since its release in 2013. Not bad for a game in which you essentially steal cars and shoot guns.

If you haven’t played the games, you should know that they take place in a sort of shadow version of the US, with each game taking place in a new city inspired by a real-world counterpart. For me, they’ve been a fascinating companion to my travels in America. When I’m in New York, walking among towering skyscrapers, I can’t help but be reminded of Liberty City, the location of 2001’s dark and atmospheric Grand Theft Auto III. On holiday in Los Angeles, driving along the Pacific Coast Highway, the long, ocean-view roads of GTA V ’s Los Santos were front of mind.

body: Microsoft has said its services have been fully restored after a worldwide outage affected several of its tools, causing disruption.
The tech firm said early on Saturday morning that efforts to address the underlying problem had been completed and customers using Outlook, Teams and Copilot should no longer be affected.
The outage hit more than 70 countries, disrupting everything from business operations to government services and personal users. More than 430 million people use the affected products worldwide.
Microsoft apologised for the technical issue, which it said was introduced during a "network capacity upgrade" and was not caused by a cyber-attack or an artificial intelligence agent.

highlights.title: Introducing ChatGPT Wallet
highlights.summary: Introducing ChatGPT Wallet, a secure way for agents in ChatGPT Work, Codex, and dots to complete purchases with user approval and existing card protections.
body: 1.2B people use ChatGPT each week, and many of them turn to it to research products, compare options, and decide what to buy. With ChatGPT Wallet, we’re now helping people complete purchases, and giving their agents a way to pay that businesses can accept with their existing systems.

To accept payment from ChatGPT Wallet, websites need to ensure agents are not inadvertently blocked, and payment and risk systems need to recognize legitimate purchases made by agents. We’re starting with limited availability to ChatGPT Pro users, so we can learn from real-world use and work with businesses, banks, and payment networks to improve compatibility and reliability.
ChatGPT Wallet gives agents a secure way to pay on a user’s behalf. Users add a card once, then approve each purchase without re-entering their payment details.

Before each purchase, the user reviews the items, total, and selected card, then approves it with a security check such as Face ID or a fingerprint scan. Each approval creates a clear record of the purchase the user authorized the agent to make.

highlights.title: Vice City was the GTA that established Rockstar's killer formula - and 24 years on, it's still one of the best games ever made
highlights.summary: "Get the limey out of here," Burt Reynolds tells the producers of GTA: Vice City during a recording session for the game, as Rockstar co-founder Dan Houser enters the studio.
body: I can't verify the truth of this story. It's one of those development rumours that's been around for a long time, originally written in a book about how games conquered pop culture called "All Your Base Are Belong to Us" by Harold Goldberg. But I like to believe it's true, because in this one moment, the two crucial strands of GTA: Vice City's DNA helix together: its star power and Rockstar's arrogance.

And I'm not saying that in a pejorative way at all. I think a game of Vice City's scope - stretched to breaking with ambition, budget, and technical wizardry - couldn't exist without the ego trip of Rockstar at its highest. This is a game that (somehow!) started as a bit of DLC for GTA 3, supposedly intended to launch as a mission pack when Rockstar North figured out how to port it to PC. GTA 3 launched in October 2001, and by some miracle - and lots of crunch, no doubt - Vice City hit shelves in October 2002.

highlights.title: Two courtrooms, one celebrity: how did the Russell Brand case compare with the rape trial next door?
highlights.summary: One was a high-profile defendant watched by more than 100 journalists. Another was an unknown man who preyed on a girl almost half his age. Their stories played out minutes apart, one entirely out of the spotlight.
body: What is going on inside Russell Brand’s head as he arrives at court for the start of his rape trial? He sees the dozens of cameras and journalists lined outside Southwark crown court, many of whom have been waiting since before 7am, and he tells himself that the media are all against him. “It seems to me that they believe that I am guilty, and that this should be the rubber-stamping of the process of my destruction.”

He walks with his wife, Laura, and his bodyguard past the photographers, “clickering, clackering, snickering paparazzi, like locusts, peculiar concoctions, not fully humans”, and up into the court, where he is suddenly overwhelmed by “the presence of something very beautiful, grace”. “In a situation like I’m in, it’s impossible not to turn to God. Truth and justice are the only things that can save me,” he thinks.

In one of the early hearings, he also receives some words of support from a court security guard, “just some normal geezer, patting me down for weapons or sharps”, who whispers: “All right, Russell. The whole country’s behind you, mate. The whole country’s behind you.”

body: On The Vergecast: The many spiraling stories in the AI world, the fate of streaming services, Mark Zuckerberg’s meat, and more.

On this episode of The Vergecast, David and Nilay start by trying to unpack the many parts of the story. We’re all going to learn a lot more about Megaspeed than we ever planned or wanted, and we’re going to hear a lot of people — particularly newly elected Democrats — asking questions about who knew what and when. In the meantime, who will replace Huang as the AI industry’s front man? And will everyone survive the scrutiny that’s coming?

After that, the hosts tackle a week filled with small-ish news from streaming services that adds up to Hollywood’s plan to properly take on TikTok. Is it the only rational thing to try? You bet. Finally, in the lightning round, it’s time for Brendan Carr Is a Dummy, Mark Zuckerberg’s AI experiments, the Cybertruck era, and more.

highlights.title: 20 Years Ago, the Best Sci-Fi Show of the Century Delivered the Most Epic Space Battle in TV History
highlights.summary: Two decades later, this spectacle from Battlestar Galactica season 3’s “Exodus, Part 2” remains unforgettable sci-fi TV. It’s dazzling and horrifying, and still one of the coolest things ever broadcast on science-fiction television.
body: To liberate the humans trapped under Cylon occupation, Admiral William Adama (Edward James Olmos) jumps the titular Battlestar Galactica directly into the atmosphere of New Caprica. The warship plummets toward the settlement and deploys Viper fighter jets amidst the chaos before jumping back into space moments before it would have crashed, likely obliterating the planet on impact.

Minutes later, while the Galactica is damaged and surrounded by enemy ships, Lee Adama (Jamie Bamber) arrives aboard the Pegasus. He buys his father enough time to escape, evacuates his own crew, and transforms the most advanced remaining warship in humanity's fleet into an enormous battering ram. Pegasus tears through one Cylon basestar, explodes, and sends a flaming flight pod spinning into another. It’s both a spectacular death scene and the decisive blow in the battle to liberate New Caprica.
